record_type_quote: Therefore, we conducted a direct replication of the literary fiction condition and the popular fiction condition from Kidd and Castano’s Experiment 5 to scrutinize the effect of reading literary fiction on ToM.

targets.title: Reading literary fiction improves theory of mind.
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, we conducted a direct replication of the literary fiction condition and the popular fiction condition from Kidd and Castano’s Experiment 5 to scrutinize the effect of reading literary fiction on ToM.
targets.outcome_quote: The results of this replication were largely consistent with Kidd and Castano’s original findings.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall author verdict about this replication as a whole determines the outcome under rule 1. The discussion also describes the present study as largely replicating the findings. The Yoni affective contrast and alternative exclusions qualify the evidence but do not replace that overall verdict. Meta-analysis outcomes concern a separate synthesis.

reasoning: New MTurk sample directly re-tests Experiment 5. Only Kidd and Castano (2013) is an original target; other replication studies enter a small meta-analysis rather than being re-tested. Earlier publication of these new data is disclosed and is not the finding targeted. P-curve examines published statistics, not a re-analysis of original participant data.
